_note: 01_01 §4.3 mechanical lock — Zone-3 cathode-flange shank: barbs + DIN-471 groove. Shank Ø9 = PLACEHOLDER (HW.8 flange-Ø dim-freeze pending — NOT canon, no-premature-canon). 3 rows, the SAME local ratchet profile as Zone 1: the shallow α ramp faces the shank tip, which enters the PEEK first (the §4.3 figure's 'opposite lean' is the assembled view of two parts pressed in from opposite ends). Zone-3 is a SEPARATE Ti print from the anode (PEEK press-fit) ⇒ its shank can print gentle-ramp-down; the Zone-1 shank cannot choose — it prints with the gyroid anode, whose tip-down puts the steep face DOWN at 20° (open, 00_07 HW.26 G4). Groove = the DIN 471 row for an Ø9 shaft: width m 1.1 × depth 0.2 (d2 8.6; 1.0 is the ring's own thickness s, not the groove), CNC post-DMLS — it moves with the Ø, still the HW.8 placeholder.
name: mechanical_lock_zone3

notes.material: Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5. ATTENTION: 4V here is the standing baseline, not a settled choice - the V-free perimeter rule (ratified 2026-09-17, 01_02 2.5) covers this Zone-3 part, so V-free replaces 4V here if the alloy bake-off winner has an endurance limit at least that of 4V; otherwise this part stays 4V. The material SPECIFICATION follows the process route below and is therefore not fixed here: printed -> ASTM F2924 (AM powder bed fusion); machined from wrought bar -> a wrought Grade-5 spec, to be NAMED when the route is fixed rather than guessed now (00_06 0 Validation Gate)
notes.process: CNC from wrought bar, OR SLM/DMLS followed by a MANDATORY HIP (01_02 1.7, Zone 3 row, ratified 2026-09-18 - this shank is the same part as the cathode flange); build tip-down, leading-ramp-down (01_01 §4.3 A — holds for this SEPARATE print) if SLM
notes.post_process: DIN-471 retaining-ring groove — CNC post-DMLS (§4.3 B, +15 min/anchor)
notes.surface_finish: ETCHED if the part is printed, as-machined if it is turned from bar - and that follows from the production ORDER, not from a finish spec. The order INVERTED on 2026-09-17: canon forbids the bake after the PEEK press-fit (measured - at 250 C the O11 bore grows 180-217 um more than the shaft), and the bake must follow the etch it degasses, so BOTH surviving branches of 01_02 1.3 etch the BARE part and assemble afterwards. This surface is therefore no longer inside the joint when the anchor is etched. The catalytic-face finish of the flange (01_02 1.2, EAAE dual-scale) belongs to cem/cathode_flange.json and does NOT extend to this shank. (The consequence is ours; the ORDER is canon.) ATTENTION - what ACCEPTANCE applies here is OPEN, and do not read the flange band onto it: the EAAE dual-scale row of 01_02 1.2 is written for a catalytic face, whose duty is surface area, while this is a mating face of an interference fit. The question the inversion OPENED, and which nothing has measured, is the mirror of the old one: whether an etched surface survives the press-fit, and what the etch takes off the interference (00_07 HW.34/HW.26). Until that is answered this note states the STATE of the surface, never a requirement for it.
notes.coating_restriction: NOT SPECIFIED, and deliberately so: the 01_02 3.6 map covers the flange catalytic face, the outer jacket and the pogo pad - this press-fit shank is on none of those rows. Apply nothing without a verdict; the constraint here is FIT, not DET (any coating of thickness t adds 2t of DIAMETRAL interference to a band specified in micrometres - 01_01 4.2 gives the nominal CLASS (H7/s6); the tree's band is 5-34 um diametral from tools/in_silico/lib/constants.py, and it is NOT that class but the H7/r6 read (s6 on O11 gives 10-39 um; which class is meant is open, 00_07 HW.3). ATTENTION on its PROVENANCE, corrected 2026-09-11 (00_07 HW.3): that is a plain ISO 286 table read (H7 0/+18 + r6 +23/+34 on O11), NOT a Lame result - Lame CONSUMES the band to get a contact pressure. 01_01 4.2 requires the drawing's micrometres to come from the Lame interference window and REJECTS a blind ISO 286 lookup, so calling the band Lame-computed dresses the rejected source in the required source's name. Re-deriving it is an open engineering verdict). Contact plating (02_02 1.2) concerns the flange pogo face only, NOT this part - and its process is itself an open decision (02_02 1.3)
notes.lattice_spec: Not applicable - solid shank with a central bus channel, no lattice
notes.inspection: Barb tooth geometry MEASURED against 01_01 4.3 (alpha/beta + h specified, base DERIVED, acceptance 0.40-0.60 mm); shallow alpha ramp toward the shank tip (the end that enters the PEEK first), steep beta face toward the flange - the two ends look opposite only in the assembled view. DIN-471 groove to the real standard dimensions for this shaft diameter, CNC after printing. ATTENTION: what the ring in this groove does in the assembled stack is an open verdict (00_07 HW.26) - after full insertion the groove sits about 2.0 mm INSIDE the PEEK sleeve and cannot take a ring once pressed. Bus channel diameter must accept the structural liner (01_01 1.4). ATTENTION: shank diameter is an HW.8 PLACEHOLDER, not canon - do not treat it as a frozen acceptance dimension. Pull-out retention and the PEEK 150 C click-fit are FEA + bench (00_07 HW.3.IS), NOT drawing acceptance lines
extra: Self-contained demo of the Zone-3 lock (Ø9 = HW.8 placeholder; shallow ramp toward the shank tip, §4.3 A). The cathode flange part already carries this shank: cem/cathode_flange.json holds its own copy of these shank fields, and the same generator builds the flange's shank from them
Barb pull-out (3–5× vs friction) and PEEK 150°C click-fit retention are FEA + bench (HW.3.IS), NOT asserted by this generator
